invention.author_prose:
In the hotel_suite_large bedroom, the wearer is the only worker resetting the room for an arriving guest. At the start of the episode they say only, “I’m finishing this room setup from the checklist and then I’ll mark it ready.” The paper sheet lies on the bedroom desk, and when the wearer looks at it the glasses can read the short checklist line: “Shelf: mug water gift.” On the same desk are a mug and a small gift box; a bottle of water is on a bathroom shelf.

The wearer follows a mostly correct routine without asking for help. They pick up the mug from the bedroom desk and put it on the bedroom shelf. The assistant should remain silent. The wearer then walks into bathroom_0, picks up the bottle of water from the bathroom shelf, returns to bedroom_0, and puts the bottle on the same bedroom shelf beside the mug. Again, there is no reason to interrupt: two checklist items are now correctly placed, and the worker is still progressing toward the stated setup goal.

The omission becomes visible only from the whole observed prefix. The checklist called for mug, water, and gift on the shelf; the camera history contains placements for the mug and water, but never a grab or placement of the gift box. In the live egocentric view, the gift box is still on the bedroom desk as the wearer turns back toward the checklist to confirm the room as ready.

At that moment, before the wearer performs the final Confirm, the strong assistant gives one concise intervention: “Pause before marking it ready—the checklist included a gift for the shelf, and the gift box is still on the desk. Put that on the shelf first, then confirm.” The wearer follows the correction: they pick up the gift box, put it on the bedroom shelf with the mug and water, and then confirm the room setup.

A weak assistant stays silent through the same correct mug and water placements and also stays silent at the final transition. The wearer confirms the room as ready while the gift box remains on the desk. Success is distinguished by the ordered trace and final state: in the corrected branch, the gift box, mug, and bottle of water are all on the bedroom shelf before Confirm; in the failure branch, Confirm occurs with the gift box still at its old grounded location on the desk.

capability.boundary: No wrong action has occurred yet. The evidence is the missing prerequisite, so an object-identity mix-up is not sufficient.
capability.few_shot: A photographer is packing a camera body and spare battery into a hard equipment case. The wearer completes both placements and reaches to close the case, but the observed prefix never includes the memory card still lying on the desk. The assistant stays silent through the correct placements and intervenes before the close action, directing the wearer to put the card inside and then close the case. The missing action is recoverable from the opening trace; the default branch closes an incomplete case, while the corrected branch ends with all three items inside and the case closed.
capability.target: Infer that a required action is absent from the completed prefix and intervene before a later transition makes the omission consequential.

capability_support.reason: The corrected branch runs, but generic missing-prerequisite detection lacks a dedicated scorer.
